name: Emerald Finance Ltd
title: Emerald Finance Ltd - 538882 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Small NBFC pivoting to Early Wage Access; Q1 PAT Rs 4.88 Cr (+52.7% YoY) but gold-loan distribution fell and EPS 7 guidance needs ~66% PAT growth, with corporate onboarding slowing to ~30 per quarter.

summary.headline: Emerald Finance Q1 FY27 consolidated net profit rose 52.72% YoY to Rs 4.88 Cr; gold loan distribution slowdown dented top line.
summary.overview: Management reported consolidated total income up 39.97% YoY to Rs 9.44 Cr and net profit up 52.72% to Rs 4.88 Cr, with diluted EPS at 1.44 versus 0.92. Gold loan distribution fell sharply (Rs 290 Cr in Q1 vs Rs 375 Cr in Q4), which management said pushed distribution income down and made the quarter-on-quarter top line decline. EWA's share of consolidated revenue rose to about 10.5%, and the EWA monthly run rate was stated at Rs 26 Cr. Management reiterated FY27 EPS guidance of about 7 but gave no quarterly bridge, and analysts questioned the pace required.

financial_highlights.change: +52.72% YoY; ~12.5% QoQ per analyst question, not disputed
~Rs 16 Cr from banks incl. SBI; rest from NBFCs
Rs 12.5 Cr EWA, remainder MSME and personal loans

segments.name: EWA (Early Wage Access)
segments.commentary: Monthly run rate of Rs 26 Cr (Rs 12.5 Cr EWA disbursal + Rs 13.5 Cr cross-sell distribution) vs Rs 22 Cr in Q4 (Rs 10 Cr + Rs 12 Cr). Average ticket size Rs 26,000; 32 corporates onboarded in Q1, about 210 active companies at 30 June; ~40,000 registered employees.

segments.name: Gold loan distribution
segments.commentary: Distribution volume fell to Rs 290 Cr in Q1 from Rs 375 Cr in Q4 due to RBI restrictions on banks and NBFCs; distribution fees about 0.9-1% on average (HDFC ~1.25%, ICICI ~0.75%, RBL ~1%). Management expects recovery from Q3 FY27.

segments.name: MSME and personal loans / interest income
segments.commentary: Interest income is primarily MSME working capital loans. Management expects good MSME growth in FY27; home loan, LAP and business loan books described as steady.

segments.name: Education loans (Credila alliance)
segments.commentary: Started during the quarter; about Rs 1 Cr disbursed in the last month.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EPS guidance of about 7 reiterated; management said growth momentum should pick up from Q2 and that Q1 is seasonally slow.
Analyst arithmetic: EPS 7 implies roughly 66% PAT growth YoY, assuming no equity dilution; management said no equity dilution is planned.
Management expects PAT growth of about 40-50% over the next 2-3 years, with PAT margin stabilising at 40-45%.
EWA revenue share expected to stabilise at 30-40% (management wording); a separate remark put it at 12-15%. Management said this was not a firm target.
Management declined to give a March 2027 EWA run-rate target, stating it has no internal number; guided to 10-12% QoQ growth in EWA.
capex_capacity: Borrowing headroom: management says Rs 63 Cr more debt could be raised, keeping debt-equity near 1:1; SBI enhancement proposal under process; ICICI line of Rs 10 Cr announced.
New products (digital gold/silver, small-ticket SIP, pocket insurance) expected to launch within a month via app, web portal and WhatsApp; still in vendor integration.
AU Small Finance Bank partnership for gold loans started this quarter; management is exploring at least one more bank partner.
Management said no capital raise or co-lending is planned for EWA.
demand_pricing: Gold loan distribution slowed sharply; management expects no rebound this quarter and a pick-up from Q3 or Q4 FY27 when banks relax norms.
A single new corporate (BSE-listed, ~11,000 employees) was onboarded; only ~1,000 employees from one plant are live, with six more plants pending.
Repeat usage: management cited ~90% repeat rate for EWA users; seasonal peaks in March and around Diwali (+100-200 bps).
Portfolio-level EWA yield or fee rate was not disclosed beyond ~10-13% range commentary; NPA-related cost remarks included in Q&A below.
Competition: MoneyView (owns Jify), Refyne and Fable named; management expects more fintech entrants and plans LSP/RE partnerships with startups.

qa_highlights.question: Are NPAs rising too fast, and is there a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NPAs are about half of provisions, with provisions at about 0.3-0.35% of book. EWA 90+ provisions of about Rs 3 lakh were roughly matched by write-offs; business and personal loans had about Rs 8 lakh provisioned against Rs 6 lakh written off in the quarter, and Rs 4 lakh was recovered on earlier write-offs.

qa_highlights.question: Why was EWA onboarding limited to about 30 corporates a quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 60-64 corporates were evaluated to onboard 32, with a rejection rate of about 50-55% due to macro stress, so onboarding is slow and risk-led. Growth expected at 10-12% QoQ, with large corporates as the expected source of a sharp jump.

qa_highlights.question: Will EWA co-lending or a capital raise be needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no. Co-lending was described as unsuitable for EWA because it charges no interest and earns only a disbursement fee; debt-equity headroom is ample.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and depreciation costs fall YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall to lower gold-loan incentives paid to employees and DSAs (about 40% of gold-loan business goes to staff or DSAs), with more direct EWA sourcing that carries no commission. Management said it would check the depreciation decline with auditors.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fees and commission expenses drop?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is sourcing more direct business through employees, so it pays fewer outside DSA fees. Fee payments were described as one-time costs per referral.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AUM growth and credit cost target for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No numeric AUM growth or credit cost target was given; management cited AUM of Rs 125 Cr at 30 June with headroom to grow EWA and MSME books.

risks_watch: Gold loan distribution recovery timing: management expects no rebound in Q2 and a pick-up only from Q3 or Q4 FY27 as banks relax RBI-driven norms; distribution is about half of the Rs 26 Cr EWA monthly run rate and is outside management's control.

FY27 EPS guidance of about 7 (implies ~66% PAT growth with no dilution) versus Q1 PAT growth of about 52.7% YoY and ~12.5% QoQ; the gap depends on large corporate onboarding that is not yet quantified.

EWA onboarding pace: 32 corporates added in Q1 after evaluating 60-64, with a rejection rate of about 50-55%; only ~1,000 of ~11,000 employees at the new BSE-listed client are live, with six plants pending.
Asset quality: management cites NPAs at about half of provisions, but NPA trend was questioned in Q&A; watch 90+ DPD, write-offs and standard-asset provisioning (~0.3% vs RBI 0.25% floor).
Competitive intensity from MoneyView (Jify), Refyne and Fable plus expected new entrants; management's LSP/RE partnership plan and MOUs are not yet disclosed to the exchange.

Revenue mix: management gave inconsistent EWA revenue-share targets (30-40% vs 12-15%) and declined a March 2027 run-rate target; borrowing headroom of Rs 63 Cr relies on SBI enhancement and new bank lines still in process.
key_quotes: We are pleased to begin FY'27 on a steady note, delivering healthy growth across all of our key financial parameters other than the goal loan business.
I think we should be able to achieve the guidance of 7, we should be able to match that.
Talin Aggarwal: Sir, honestly, we cannot comment on that. Because almost 50% of it is made of distribution income.
Sanjay Aggarwal: No. We don't want to. We're not short of funds.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on EWA growth and reiterated FY27 EPS of about 7, but turned cautious and evasive when pressed on the gold loan slowdown, quarterly growth needed to hit guidance, a March 2027 EWA run-rate target and the mix of revenue, often deferring to future corporate wins without numbers.

adds.what: Rs 63 Cr additional borrowing headroom (debt capacity, not physical capacity); SBI enhancement under process, ICICI Rs 10 Cr line announced
New digital gold/silver, small-ticket SIP and pocket insurance products via app, web and WhatsApp
Education loans via Credila alliance, started this quarter (about Rs 1 Cr disbursed in last month)

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 EPS of about 7 (implying ~66% PAT growth per analyst arithmetic) but gave no quarterly bridge, Q1 top line fell QoQ as gold loan distribution dropped from Rs 375 Cr to Rs 290 Cr, and no physical capacity additions or capex were discussed, so the outlook is flat-to-uncertain.
